justification: Closes the three actionable deferrals from the enrichment plan: SEPP-over-LEP override banners now cite the clause of the standards row that grants the overriding value; the brief gains a Solar Potential card that fires the SAME rate-limited route the standalone solar tool already uses in production (no inline paid API calls); and the scheduled contract-drift check exists as a runner script plus Railway config-as-code, dry-run verified live.

pre_impl.existing_data: The solar pipeline (services/solar_yield.py, Google Solar API) is already live behind the rate-limited /api/satellite/solar-yield route in the reports hub, so the production key exists; fetch_sepp_housing_standards rows already carry source_clause and source_document per standard; the drift checker and capture logic already exist from Slice 0 — only the scheduled runner was missing.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: My earlier claim that solar was blocked on a missing key described only the dev box — the standalone tool works in production, so the brief card was wired via the granny-flat marker pattern. The drift cron's first draft included the bushfire capture; that was removed because run_bushfire persists a report row and a cron must never write junk rows into production data.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: The solar card fires the EXISTING gated route (billing, rate limits and future Stripe gating stay in one place — the brief never calls the paid API inline; the backend emits only a marker slot like granny flat). The cron runner composes the two existing drift tools; the citation work threads existing row fields through the existing grouping, no new source.

functions.name: _fetch_solar_marker
functions.output: the decoupled marker dict that reserves the solar card slot in the stream
functions.if_none: a test asserts the function contains no requests or key usage, so the paid API can never be invoked inline by the brief

functions.name: _build_sepp_housing
functions.input: the standards rows including each row's source_clause and source_document
functions.output: SEPPStandard entries carrying the height and FSR granting-row citations
functions.if_none: a dev type whose granting row has no citation yields citation fields of None — no fabricated clause

functions.name: _detect_sepp_lep_overrides
functions.input: the eligible standards with their per-control citations plus the LEP height and FSR
functions.output: SeppLepOverride rows whose source_clause is the clause of the row that grants the overriding value
functions.if_none: no citation on the granting row leaves source_clause None and the banner renders without a clause — never an invented reference

functions.name: main
functions.input: live captures from the read-only services the brief consumes (strata cadastre, climate)
functions.output: exit 0 on contract, exit 1 with a Telegram alert on drift or capture failure
functions.if_none: a harness crash itself pages Telegram and exits 1 — the cron can never fail silently

values.value: coverage_available flag from the Google Solar response
values.if_missing: false renders an explicit no-imagery-coverage state; a transport error renders the retry state — neither is a data claim

queries: N/A — no new database queries; the drift cron is read-only by design (report-writing services excluded)

break_it.scenario: A refactor makes the brief call the paid Google Solar API inline during assembly
break_it.what_happens: The marker-only design is pinned: a test inspects _fetch_solar_marker's source for any requests or key usage and fails the suite

break_it.scenario: An override banner shows a SEPP value increase with no clause behind it
break_it.what_happens: The citation rides from the standards row that grants the overriding value; when that row has no clause the banner simply omits the reference — no citation, no claim, and never a fabricated one

break_it.scenario: Someone adds the bushfire capture back into the drift cron
break_it.what_happens: run_bushfire persists a property report row, so a weekly cron would write junk rows into production data — a source-scan test fails on any report-writing service in the runner

break_it.scenario: Google Solar has no imagery at the address
break_it.what_happens: coverage_available false renders the explicit no-imagery state — distinct from a failed request, which renders the retry state
break_it.how: three rendered states in SolarBriefCard plus the derived loading state
break_it.repro: run the brief with satellite for a rural address without Solar coverage

break_it.scenario: The drift cron itself crashes (import error, network down)
break_it.what_happens: The crash handler pages Telegram with the traceback and exits 1 — the schedule can never rot silently
break_it.how: top-level except in run_brief_drift_check.py; dry-run verified live (2 services on contract, exit 0)

post_merge.secrets: none in code; the cron service needs DATABASE_URL, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID set in the Railway dashboard
post_merge.manual_verify: Railway: create service brief-drift-check from this repo, point Config Path at railway.brief-drift.toml, set the env vars (CLI session expired mid-creation — needs railway login). Then run the brief with satellite for Concord: the Solar Potential card fires the existing route and renders panel capacity and yield
